description.narrative: The project will improve domestic transport connectivity in Fiji by replacing four critical bridges on the country's main island with newly constructed bridges resilient to climate change and disasters. The project will enhance the capacity of FRA in asset management and preparing gender-responsive policies and investments. The project will also prepare an upstream, transport sector-wide multi-hazard and gender vulnerability assessment and an investment road map, including the preparation of at least one transport-related investment with innovative solutions to build resilience among the poorest and most vulnerable segments of the population.

Output: Critical bridges replaced with new resilient bridges Indicator: Four critical bridges across Fiji replaced with newly constructed bridges to withstand the impacts of climate change and disasters Progress/Status: The Detailed Engineering Design for the four bridges was completed in April 2024.
Civil works, bidding for Packages A and B Closed on 30 April 2025, with five submissions received. Draft Technical Bid Evaluation Report (TBER) was submitted to ADB on 16 July 2025. Following joint reviews with PPFD, ADB issued first round of comments on 12 August and the revised TBER was resubmitted to ADB on the 27 August 2025. After further review, ADB issued second round of comments on the 2 October 2025, requesting FRA to reassess scoring for one bidder slightly below the minimum technical threshold. FRA subsequently reassessed and confirmed the evaluation results with no change and formally communicated its position to ADB on 9 October 2025. ADB NOL to proceed to financial evaluation was issued on 3 November 2025. 7 November 2025, FRA advised ADB that price bids were no longer available on Tenderlink due to FRA's 90 days document storage period.
On 19 December 2025, MOF requested on agreed way forward to rebid, invite only technical qualified bidders. ADB responded to MOF on 23 December 2025 to notify bidders and cancel bid, update procurement plan and update procurement method to LCB. Notice of technical scores and annul tender was issued to bidders on 23 & 24 December 2025. Draft bidding documents was submitted to ADB on 14 January 2026. ADB's comments were sent to FRA on 19 January 2026 and awaiting response from FRA.
Consulting services Proposals for the Construction Supervision Consultant (CSC) closed on 19 May 2025, with technical and financial evaluations completed and negotiations with the first-ranked firm concluded in September 2025. The draft contract (approx. US$12 million) incorporating negotiated comments is under FRA legal review, with signing expected by Q1 2026. For the project management unit consists of eight (8) individual positions to assist FRA with managing the works. Project Manager's contract was signed on 7 November 2025. Two roles—Social Safeguards Specialist, and Portfolio/Contract Manager—are being finalized and signing targeted by Q1 2026. Other remaining positions are at various stages of recruitment, while the Environmental Safeguards Specialist position will be re-advertised. Full PMU mobilization is required before commencement of civil works.
